findings.summary: The anonymous default fixes the site to light mode instead of following the operating-system color preference.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the probe reported a light body (rgb(248,249,250)), color-scheme: normal, and the screenshot remained visually identical to light mode. The Appearance panel shows Light selected even though an Automatic option exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Make Automatic the anonymous default, declare color-scheme: light dark, and apply the existing dark tokens whenever prefers-color-scheme is dark.

findings.summary: Primary cross-document navigation changes state abruptly without a declarative view transition.
findings.evidence: The recorded homepage-to-Moscow search flow completes, but the CSS probe found no view-transition rules and the video shows a direct page swap.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an opt-in cross-document View Transition for same-origin navigation, while retaining the existing no-motion fallback and reduced-motion override.

findings.summary: The pages advertise a fixed 1120px viewport, causing desktop layouts and tiny text to be scaled into narrow mobile screens.
findings.evidence: Every page probe reported meta viewport content="width=1120". At a 360x800 device viewport, layout measured a 1120 to 1294 CSS-pixel viewport and the screenshots show a full desktop article scaled to unreadably small text.
findings.suggestedFix: Use width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and responsive breakpoints; reflow sidebars, infoboxes, controls and content instead of shrinking a fixed-width canvas.

findings.summary: Many inline links and citation controls are too small or tightly spaced for touch.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size; examples include a 60x16 History link and 12x12 citation links. The page probe lists many 14 to 17px-high interactive targets.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase line-height and interactive padding/spacing so common targets provide at least 24x24 CSS pixels, with 44px targets for primary controls.

findings.summary: The representative article misses the good LCP range under Lighthouse mobile conditions.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 4.5s, LCP 4.5s, Speed Index 5.7s and performance 0.71. Layout also observed a 459ms main-thread task during article startup, although CLS stayed near zero and TBT was only 50ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, reduce startup work, prioritise the LCP content, and defer nonessential modules until after the initial article render.

findings.summary: Short-lived cache entries and render-blocking styles add avoidable work to article startup.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified three render-blocking stylesheets and estimated 54 KiB savings from efficient cache lifetimes; key ResourceLoader CSS and startup JS had five-minute cache lifetimes.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate critical styles from deferred modules, preload only discovered critical resources, and use long immutable caching for versioned ResourceLoader responses.

findings.summary: The article ships substantial JavaScript and CSS unused during the measured load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 162 KiB of unused JavaScript and 89 KiB of unused CSS, including a roughly 400 KiB ResourceLoader JavaScript response.
findings.suggestedFix: Split article-reading essentials from editing, media, survey and enhancement modules, then load optional modules on interaction or visibility.

findings.summary: The mobile navigation toggle lacks a usable label in the accessibility tree, and an infobox uses a fake table caption.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.89 and failed label because the checkbox references an aria-hidden label. It also failed table-fake-caption because the Russia infobox starts with a colspan cell instead of caption.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the menu control a non-hidden accessible name and use a real caption element for infobox table titles.

findings.summary: Inline links rely on color alone and do not reach 3:1 contrast against surrounding text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed link-in-text-block on article links such as “Россия (значения)”, reporting only 1.32:1 contrast against surrounding text and no persistent non-color styling.
findings.suggestedFix: Underline inline content links by default or adjust link color to reach 3:1 against surrounding text while preserving text/background contrast.

findings.summary: Some article images lack dimensions or useful alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed unsized-images. The article probe found 277 images, 73 without an alt attribute and one without complete width/height attributes; category and 404 templates also each had one image missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height for every image and ensure meaningful content images have concise alt text while decorative images use alt="".

findings.summary: Large first-party bundles lack valid source maps and Chrome recorded Inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed valid-source-maps and inspector-issues for the representative article.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish valid production source maps for large first-party bundles and clear the Chrome Issues panel findings in release validation.

findings.summary: Public article and listing templates omit meta descriptions, and structured/share metadata is inconsistent across templates.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-description. Probes found no description on homepage, Russia article, category, Moscow article or 404; the category also had no JSON-LD and only og:title/og:type, while the article had JSON-LD and an OG image.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate concise, template-specific meta descriptions and consistent Open Graph/structured metadata from the article or category lead.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS and HSTS-protected, but browser defenses are weakened by a broad unsafe CSP, missing policies and one insecure first-party session identifier cookie.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP with unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval plus broad source lists, no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors. Cookie audit found ruwikimwuser-sessionId without Secure and with SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Tighten CSP with nonces/hashes and frame-ancestors, add explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and set Secure with an appropriate SameSite mode on every session identifier.

findings.summary: Search inputs explicitly disable browser autocomplete.
findings.evidence: DOM probes across templates found autocomplete="off" on the primary search input, despite search being a repeated, non-sensitive task.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow browser history/autofill for non-sensitive search terms unless a documented privacy requirement requires disabling it.

findings.summary: The reading view downloads roughly a quarter-megabyte of code and styles unused in the measured journey.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 162 KiB unused JavaScript and 89 KiB unused CSS. Total transfer was otherwise proportionate at 934 KiB and no autoplay media or known trackers were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate editing, survey, media and enhancement modules behind interaction or visibility and set a reading-template unused-code budget.

findings.summary: Wikipedia is highly relevant to agents and serves crawlable structured content, but exposes no explicit safe agent capabilities for search or article operations.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 100% raw-HTML content coverage and article JSON-LD is present, but probes found no WebMCP or agentic tool registration.
findings.suggestedFix: Explore narrowly scoped, read-only agent tools for search and article retrieval with clear schemas, rate limits and privacy boundaries.

taskList.title: Replace the fixed 1120px viewport with true responsive reflow and touch-sized controls
Fix menu naming, infobox captions, link distinction and image alternatives
Improve article LCP and defer unused reading-view modules
Tighten CSP, browser policies and cookie security attributes
Make operating-system color scheme the anonymous default
Add consistent meta descriptions and structured sharing metadata
Address source-map/Inspector hygiene and search input assistance
Explore progressive cross-document transitions and read-only agent tools
